chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a, who said: I asked him
about the sheep that one slaughters while in its belly is a young one that has already grown hair. So he (peace be upon him) said: Its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother.

key_terms.أَشْعَرَ: grown hair — the condition whereby the fetus has developed body hair, indicating sufficient development; this is the condition that triggers the ruling
key_terms.ذَكَاة: ritual slaughter (zakah) — the Islamic method of slaughtering an animal to render it halal, involving cutting the throat with a sharp blade while invoking God's name

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on a fetus found inside a slaughtered animal?
ai.summary: Sama'a ibn Mihran narrates that he asked Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the ruling for a fetus found in the womb of a slaughtered sheep that had already developed hair. The Imam ruled that the slaughter of the mother constitutes the slaughter of the fetus as well, meaning the fetus is permissible to eat without a separate act of slaughter. This ruling is a fundamental principle in Islamic jurisprudence regarding the legality of consuming fetal animals.
